entities.summary: Gaspar Correia was a Portuguese historian and cartographer best known for his seminal work Lendas da Índia (Tales of the Indies), published in 1518, which chronicled the early history of the Portuguese Empire in Asia. This foundational text, written during the height of the Age of Exploration, provided a detailed account of the Portuguese conquest of Goa, Malacca, and other Indian Ocean trade centers, offering insights into the complex web of cultural, economic, and political relationships between Portugal and its Asian colonies. Correia's work not only served as a primary source for later historians but also influenced the development of cartography, as he produced detailed maps of the Indian Ocean region, including the coastlines of present-day India, Southeast Asia, and East Africa. The impact of Lendas da Índia extended beyond the realm of history, as it helped shape the Portuguese perception of their colonial expansion and the cultural identity of their Asian territories. Correia's legacy can be seen in the work of later historians, such as Fernão Lopes de Castanheda, who built upon his research to create a more comprehensive narrative of the Portuguese Empire's Asian adventures.
